current_claims.text: In the corrected simulator the controller that trusts its predictor is the worst controller; gated controllers stay close to data-local placement.

Single-stream decode is 50-300x memory-bound on H100 specs; prefill becomes compute-bound at 316 tokens (Llama 3.1 8B bf16), 300 (70B bf16), 80 (8B int4 weights-only). Computed from specs, configuration-specific.
MoE crossover batch about 9.9x (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and 3.7x (Mixtral-8x7B) that of a dense twin, under uniform routing and 8-position speculative verification. Theoretical estimate, not measured.
The proved break-even accuracy (u+gamma)/(1+u) matches a queueing simulation up to link utilisation of about 0.5 and breaks above.
One free-tier Tesla T4 run: 276 GB/s, 24.9 fp16 TFLOPS, roofline about 1.4x optimistic in the memory-bound regime. One run; not an H100.

Orchestrator prototype with simulated tiers: prediction halves P99 on a predictable workload and can double it on an unpredictable one; the congestion-aware gate trails a static threshold on predictable traffic. Simulated, assumed parameters, CXL is a model only.
22 Lean 4 theorem declarations about the additive model and the prefetch threshold; true inside the model.

unproven: benefit of adaptive orchestration on real workloads
